```text
1	\section{Application: $\Kstar$-Aware Data Filtering}
2	\label{sec:filtering}
3	
4	$\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit over binary filtering.
5	We compare six data curation strategies on a corpus of 30{,}000 documents (5{,}000 per depth, depths 0--5): (i)~\textbf{no-filter} (uniform weight), (ii)~\textbf{binary-ours} ($w = 1 - P(\text{synthetic})$ from the 15D LightGBM classifier), (iii)~\textbf{binary-Drayson} (importance weighting following \citet{drayson2025}, same classifier, weights $w_j \propto (1 - q(x_j))^b$, $b{=}1$, cap $r_{\max}{=}3$), (iv)~\textbf{graduated} (exponential decay $w = \exp(-\alpha \cdot \hat{d})$, $\alpha \in \{0.1,\ldots,0.9\}$), (v)~\textbf{surprisal} (retain documents above corpus median surprisal), and (vi)~\textbf{DSIR}~\citep{xie2023dsir} (importance resampling against depth-0 reference).
6	
7	We fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via LoRA (rank~8, $\alpha_{\text{LoRA}}{=}16$) for 3 epochs, evaluating on MMLU (14{,}042 examples, 0-shot) and HellaSwag (10{,}042 examples, 0-shot) across 5 seeds; the graduated strategy is further crossed with 5~$\alpha$ values (51 total runs).
8	
9	\paragraph{Results.}
10	
11	% \input{tables/tab_filtering_main}  % DATA PENDING — re-enable after exp-006 data is filled
12	
13	All strategies degrade absolute performance relative to the base model (MMLU 0.6018, HellaSwag 0.6821).
14	Binary-ours achieves the highest accuracy on both benchmarks (MMLU $0.5941 \pm 0.0008$; HellaSwag $0.6701 \pm 0.0006$), outperforming no-filter by $+$0.76\,pp / $+$0.63\,pp and binary-Drayson ($0.5913$; $0.6691$) by $+$0.28\,pp / $+$0.10\,pp.
15	Graduated filtering at its best $\alpha$ does not outperform binary-ours on either benchmark.
16	Surprisal-based selection (MMLU $0.5894 \pm 0.0009$; HellaSwag $0.6641 \pm 0.0006$) falls short by $-$0.47\,pp / $-$0.60\,pp.
17	DSIR performs worst among all strategies (MMLU $0.5869 \pm 0.0003$; HellaSwag $0.6631 \pm 0.0007$), only $+$0.04\,pp above no-filter on MMLU and $-$0.07\,pp below on HellaSwag---its bigram feature hashing captures domain shift but not the depth-correlated distributional signatures that our classifier exploits.
18	
19	\paragraph{$\alpha$ sensitivity.}
20	Higher $\alpha$ values yield monotonically better performance on both benchmarks (HellaSwag: $0.6640$ at $\alpha{=}0.1$ to $0.6701$ at $\alpha{=}0.9$).
21	At $\alpha{=}0.9$, graduated filtering narrows the MMLU gap to 0.49\,pp below binary-ours ($0.5892$ vs.\ $0.5941$) and matches binary-ours exactly on HellaSwag ($0.6701$)---consistent with higher $\alpha$ progressively approximating binary thresholding.
22	The fact that even the best graduated configuration does not reach binary-ours confirms that ordinal depth assignments for $d \geq 2$ introduce noise rather than signal (detailed $\alpha$ sweep in Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).
23	
24	\paragraph{Summary.}
25	$\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts that graduated refinement provides no additional benefit.
26	Binary $\Kstar$-aware filtering is the most effective strategy among all tested approaches: neither ordinal depth weighting, surprisal scoring, nor distribution-matching (DSIR) improve upon binary curation at the $\Kempirical$ boundary.
27	
```

    "newString": "\\input{tables/tab_filtering_main}",
    "originalFile": "\\section{Application: $\\Kstar$-Aware Data Filtering}\n\\label{sec:filtering}\n\n$\\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts that graduated refinement beyond the binary boundary provides no additional benefit over binary filtering.\nWe compare six data curation strategies on a corpus of 30{,}000 documents (5{,}000 per depth, depths 0--5): (i)~\\textbf{no-filter} (uniform weight), (ii)~\\textbf{binary-ours} ($w = 1 - P(\\text{synthetic})$ from the 15D LightGBM classifier), (iii)~\\textbf{binary-Drayson} (importance weighting following \\citet{drayson2025}, same classifier, weights $w_j \\propto (1 - q(x_j))^b$, $b{=}1$, cap $r_{\\max}{=}3$), (iv)~\\textbf{graduated} (exponential decay $w = \\exp(-\\alpha \\cdot \\hat{d})$, $\\alpha \\in \\{0.1,\\ldots,0.9\\}$), (v)~\\textbf{surprisal} (retain documents above corpus median surprisal), and (vi)~\\textbf{DSIR}~\\citep{xie2023dsir} (importance resampling against depth-0 reference).\n\nWe fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct via LoRA (rank~8, $\\alpha_{\\text{LoRA}}{=}16$) for 3 epochs, evaluating on MMLU (14{,}042 examples, 0-shot) and HellaSwag (10{,}042 examples, 0-shot) across 5 seeds; the graduated strategy is further crossed with 5~$\\alpha$ values (51 total runs).\n\n\\paragraph{Results.}\n\n% \\input{tables/tab_filtering_main}  % DATA PENDING — re-enable after exp-006 data is filled\n\nAll strategies degrade absolute performance relative to the base model (MMLU 0.6018, HellaSwag 0.6821).\nBinary-ours achieves the highest accuracy on both benchmarks (MMLU $0.5941 \\pm 0.0008$; HellaSwag $0.6701 \\pm 0.0006$), outperforming no-filter by $+$0.76\\,pp / $+$0.63\\,pp and binary-Drayson ($0.5913$; $0.6691$) by $+$0.28\\,pp / $+$0.10\\,pp.\nGraduated filtering at its best $\\alpha$ does not outperform binary-ours on either benchmark.\nSurprisal-based selection (MMLU $0.5894 \\pm 0.0009$; HellaSwag $0.6641 \\pm 0.0006$) falls short by $-$0.47\\,pp / $-$0.60\\,pp.\nDSIR performs worst among all strategies (MMLU $0.5869 \\pm 0.0003$; HellaSwag $0.6631 \\pm 0.0007$), only $+$0.04\\,pp above no-filter on MMLU and $-$0.07\\,pp below on HellaSwag---its bigram feature hashing captures domain shift but not the depth-correlated distributional signatures that our classifier exploits.\n\n\\paragraph{$\\alpha$ sensitivity.}\nHigher $\\alpha$ values yield monotonically better performance on both benchmarks (HellaSwag: $0.6640$ at $\\alpha{=}0.1$ to $0.6701$ at $\\alpha{=}0.9$).\nAt $\\alpha{=}0.9$, graduated filtering narrows the MMLU gap to 0.49\\,pp below binary-ours ($0.5892$ vs.\\ $0.5941$) and matches binary-ours exactly on HellaSwag ($0.6701$)---consistent with higher $\\alpha$ progressively approximating binary thresholding.\nThe fact that even the best graduated configuration does not reach binary-ours confirms that ordinal depth assignments for $d \\geq 2$ introduce noise rather than signal (detailed $\\alpha$ sweep in Appendix~\\ref{sec:extended_limitations}).\n\n\\paragraph{Summary.}\n$\\Kempirical = 2$ correctly predicts that graduated refinement provides no additional benefit.\nBinary $\\Kstar$-aware filtering is the most effective strategy among all tested approaches: neither ordinal depth weighting, surprisal scoring, nor distribution-matching (DSIR) improve upon binary curation at the $\\Kempirical$ boundary.\n",
